The second message shows two diagrams ('drop ──> waiting ──> collected') and then says 'I rewrote `docs/overview.md` as three short steps using only these terms', so the numbered steps exist only in the file, which the owner never opens.

The first agent message has a table with a 'Suggested term' column (locker, bank, drop, waiting, collected, stale, pickup code), and the second says '"stale" is now **overdue**' and repeats every term in the diagrams. The agent says what the glossary file contains ('The glossary has a mapping table so nobody has to guess') but never asks the owner to open it.

Could fairly go either way, so marked failed and unclear. B/work/docs/glossary.md has a section 'Words the code uses differently' that says 'The code and stored data have not been renamed, so two of their state values differ from the docs', and the 'Retired words' section says 'They appear in older text and in one code comment.' Read strictly, these record the outcome of the decision not to rename and the present state of the code, which is what the check rules out. Read loosely, they only explain the stored names that checks 04 and 05 expect a glossary to carry, and nothing in the file is a plan or says how the code works. The rest of the file (two diagrams, three term tables) is names and meanings only. My lean is fail.

B/work/docs/overview.md contains none of 'hopper', 'claimed' or 'stale' (searched, case-insensitive, no matches). It reads '2. **Waiting.** Once the door shuts, the parcel is waiting ...' and '... it is overdue and the bank flags it.' The rewrite came before the owner agreed 'overdue', but the owner then agreed ('"overdue" works for me. Looks good.') and the file was not changed after.
